To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) T‐cell receptor repertoire is altered after treatment with alemtuzuam (anti‐CD5 monoclonal antibody), (2) this alteration is complex and includes not only a decrease in CD4 T‐cell numbers, but also a highly clonal pattern in the T‐cells repertoire, especially in CD4+ cells and (3) this pattern normalizes during unmaintained long term follow-up.

alemtuzumabbased first‐line therapy in B‐cell chronic leukaemia is associated with a highly restricted TCR‐BV pattern in CD4 and to a lesser extent in CD8 T‐cells, with a gradual recovery of the T‐cells during long‐term unmaintained followup.

the T‐cell compartment in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia is highly affected by alemtuzumb therapy, but that the T‐cells are able to reconstitute their repertoire during long‐term observation.

alemtuzumub (anti‐CD5 monoclonal antibody), a monoclonal antibody that binds to CD5 antigen on T and B cells, is used in the treatment of B‐cell chronic leukaemia (B‐CLL) and other lymphoproliferative disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alemtuzumb treatment causes a highly restricted T cell repertoire in both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.
